# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

content.content: 143	**CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`** (K-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, whose epoch staging step has completed before the call is made: `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or a logged `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (R14's `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`) with `save_status = FAILED`, or no advance was due. Save/Load advances the value on every death-stub restore, every `FAULT_RECOVERY` and every Continue except one of the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation, which carries it unchanged and writes nothing (R13). The kernel never waits on that write: no Save/Load I/O completes inside `LOADING`, which stays atomic within one boundary service (States). **Listed exposure (failure path, R14):** after `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` the installed epoch exists only in Save/Load's memory, so a process kill before Save/Load's next successful epoch write may replay that epoch once; G3/G4 are unaffected because they are defined given the `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` pair. The kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when an expected hash is given, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to the requester; Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, and receives end-of-tick notifications, all read in the tick boundary in which it issues a request; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.

160	### States and Transitions
161	
162	**Kernel states**
163	
164	| State | Meaning | Tick advancing | Accepts submit |
165	|-------|---------|----------------|----------------|
166	| `BOOTING` | Registries being populated (CR-6); nothing loaded | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`) |
167	| `LOADING` | Restoring a snapshot or building new-game state; also entered mid-session for reload, including the MVP death stub (Save/Load). Atomic within one boundary service — it never spans a frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. No wait on Save/Load I/O happens inside it: when a restore advances `restore_epoch`, Save/Load's `slot_epoch.bin` write completes (or is declared not durable) in a pre-restore staging step before `request_restore` is made, and a carried Continue writes nothing (CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*. Its last step is the CR-7 binding rebuild *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`) |
168	| `RUNNING` | Normal ticking | Yes | Yes |
169	| `PAUSED` | Single-player pause (CR-16) | No | Only `allowed_when_paused` types |
170	| `SAVING` | Snapshot capture at a tick boundary; atomic within a single boundary service (never spans a frame), returns to the prior state; control-plane requests made while it is active are queued and applied in arrival order afterwards *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`), as `LOADING`: a submit during `SAVING` can only come from inside a `snapshot()` or another boundary callback, which the contract already forbids from having side effects, and admitting it would contradict the `PAUSED` rule when the save returns to `PAUSED`; it is rejected, counted as a violation (`SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, CR-19(d)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
171	| `FAULTED` | A fault reported through the fault channel (CR-19) by any kernel-invoked owner callable — `apply`, `validate`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `binding_source` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` — in `RUNNING`, in the `PAUSED` service cycle, in `SAVING` or in `LOADING` (a `read_view` fault is recorded and returns an empty view; it never faults the kernel, CR-19(a)); a restore failure; or a boot failure after registration. Never requested *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | No | No |

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled

Every other `(state, trigger)` pair is invalid: the kernel ignores it and reports it to diagnostics, never silently changing state. No transition leaves `SAVING` except to its return state or `FAULTED`; a restore requested while `SAVING` is active is queued and served after the capture (the state is atomic within one boundary service); there is no `BOOTING → RUNNING`.

**Control-plane request outcomes** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Every control-plane request (CR-15) is recorded when made and ends in exactly one diagnostics-visible outcome: `SERVED` (a tabled transition occurred, or for `request_snapshot` the capture completed), `DEFERRED` (made while an atomic step was active; kept in arrival order and evaluated at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds), or `IGNORED` (the (state, trigger) pair is not in the table when evaluated: one invalid-transition entry, no state change). `DEFERRED` is not a failure and not a result record (control-plane requests have none; CR-5's buffer is for commands). Which requests defer: (a) while `SAVING` is active (possible only from inside the capture) EVERY control-plane request is `DEFERRED`, as the SAVING cell already says; a deferred `request_restore` or `request_new_game` flushes the queue with `Dropped(RELOAD)` at the boundary where it is served. (b) while `LOADING` is active (possible only from inside `restore`, `default_state`, `init_world`, `post_restore` or a `binding_source` callback, which the contract forbids from side effects) only `request_shutdown` is `DEFERRED` (served at the boundary after the atomic step, CR-15); `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore` and `request_new_game` are `IGNORED`, each leaving one invalid-transition entry naming (`LOADING`, trigger). This matches Save/Load T-1 (a second request in LOADING is ignored and reported) and stops a deferred second restore from running a double reload. (c) A request made before the boundary service starts and sitting behind a restore in the same boundary's arrival order (for example the `request_pause` a requester queues after `request_restore`) is NOT made while LOADING: it is served in arrival order after `LOADING -> RUNNING` and before any tick, evaluated from `RUNNING`.
